templates.text: High baseline arousal with a pronounced excitatory bias in neural circuits, leading to rapid, full-body startles at minor stimuli.

Cortisol reactivity appears elevated, contributing to a high state of readiness and exaggerated motor responses to routine handling.
Neural excitability is high; the infant transitions from sleep to a full cry with a latency of under {seconds} seconds following a disturbance.
Manifests a high arousal baseline, with limb movements becoming large-amplitude and disorganized even during quiet alert states.
The cry has a high-pitched, urgent onset, reflecting an underlying neural state where inhibitory modulation is insufficient.
High cortical excitability is evident; visual or auditory stimuli easily breach a low threshold, triggering pronounced arousal and fussing.
